title: Acts Chapter 18 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Acts chapter 18 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Acts Chapter 18 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Acts Chapter 18.

questions.question: In Acts 18, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Silas and Timotheus came from Macedonia
questions.explanation: This is the first event mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Acts 18:1.

questions.question: Who did Paul meet in Corinth?
questions.explanation: Paul found a certain Jew named Aquila and his wife Priscilla in Acts 18:2.

questions.question: What was the occupation of Paul, Aquila, and Priscilla?
questions.explanation: They were of the same craft, as stated in Acts 18:3.

questions.question: In the synagogue, who did Paul persuade?
questions.explanation: Paul reasoned and persuaded both Jews and Greeks in Acts 18:4.

questions.question: What did Paul testify to the Jews when Silas and Timotheus arrived?
questions.explanation: Paul testified that Jesus was the Christ in Acts 18:5.

questions.question: What did Paul do when the Jews opposed him?
questions.explanation: Paul shook his raiment as a sign of disapproval in Acts 18:6.

questions.question: Whose house did Paul enter after leaving the synagogue?
questions.explanation: Paul entered the house of Justus, who worshipped God, as noted in Acts 18:7.

questions.question: Who believed on the Lord along with his house?
questions.explanation: Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with his house in Acts 18:8.

questions.question: What did the Lord say to Paul in a vision?
questions.explanation: The Lord told Paul to be not afraid in Acts 18:9.

questions.question: What assurance did the Lord give to Paul?
options: I have much people in this city
questions.correctAnswer: I have much people in this city
questions.explanation: The Lord assured Paul that He had much people in the city in Acts 18:10.

questions.question: Did Paul work as a tentmaker in Corinth?
questions.explanation: Paul abode with Aquila and Priscilla and worked as a tentmaker as stated in Acts 18:3.

questions.question: Did Crispus believe alone?
questions.explanation: Crispus believed on the Lord with all his house, as mentioned in Acts 18:8.

questions.question: Did Paul testify that Jesus was the Christ?
questions.explanation: Paul testified to the Jews that Jesus was Christ as stated in Acts 18:5.

questions.question: Did the Lord tell Paul he would be harmed in Corinth?
questions.explanation: The Lord assured Paul that no man would set on him to hurt him in Acts 18:10.

questions.question: Was Paul afraid to preach in Corinth?
questions.explanation: The Lord told Paul not to be afraid and to speak, indicating he was encouraged to preach, as seen in Acts 18:9.

medium.title: Acts Chapter 18 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Acts Chapter 18 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How long did Paul continue teaching in Corinth?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:11 states that Paul continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.

questions.question: What does Acts 18:12 promise will happen if someone speaks boldly as Paul did in Acts 18:9?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:12 shows that the Jews made insurrection against Paul, indicating that bold speaking can lead to opposition.

questions.question: What accusation did the Jews bring against Paul?
options: He persuaded men to worship God contrary to the law
questions.correctAnswer: He persuaded men to worship God contrary to the law
questions.explanation: Acts 18:13 states that the Jews accused Paul of persuading men to worship God contrary to the law.

questions.question: What does Acts 18:14 indicate about Gallio's reaction to the accusations against Paul?
options: He refused to judge the matter
questions.correctAnswer: He refused to judge the matter
questions.explanation: In Acts 18:15, Gallio states he will not be a judge of such matters, showing he refused to intervene.

questions.question: What did Gallio do to the Jews who accused Paul?
options: He drove them from the judgment seat
questions.correctAnswer: He drove them from the judgment seat
questions.explanation: Acts 18:16 states that Gallio drove them from the judgment seat, indicating his dismissal of their charges.

questions.question: What happened to Sosthenes after Gallio's judgment?
options: He was beaten by the Greeks
questions.correctAnswer: He was beaten by the Greeks
questions.explanation: Acts 18:17 reveals that the Greeks took Sosthenes and beat him before the judgment seat.

questions.question: Why did Paul shave his head in Cenchrea?
options: He was following a Jewish custom
questions.explanation: Acts 18:18 specifies that Paul had shorn his head in Cenchrea because he had a vow.

questions.question: What did Paul do after leaving Corinth?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:18 indicates that Paul sailed into Syria after leaving Corinth.

questions.question: What did Paul do when he arrived in Ephesus?
options: He reasoned with the Jews in the synagogue
questions.correctAnswer: He reasoned with the Jews in the synagogue
questions.explanation: Acts 18:19 states that Paul entered into the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews upon arriving in Ephesus.

questions.question: What does Acts 18:20 imply about Paul's willingness to stay in Ephesus?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:20 shows that Paul did not consent to stay longer in Ephesus, indicating he left immediately.

questions.question: What lesson can we learn from Paul's perseverance in teaching despite opposition?
options: To remain silent in difficult times
To be bold in sharing our faith
questions.correctAnswer: To be bold in sharing our faith
questions.explanation: Paul's continued teaching in the face of opposition teaches us to be bold in sharing our faith, as seen in Acts 18:11 and 18:12.

questions.question: How should we respond to situations where our faith is challenged, as Paul did?
questions.explanation: Paul reasoned with the Jews, which demonstrates the importance of calmly explaining our beliefs in challenging situations, as seen in Acts 18:19.

questions.question: Is it true that Gallio showed concern for the charges brought against Paul?
questions.explanation: Gallio cared for none of those things, indicating he showed no concern for the charges against Paul (Acts 18:17).

questions.question: Is it true that Paul was afraid to speak in Ephesus?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:9 shows that the Lord encouraged Paul not to be afraid, suggesting he was not afraid to speak in Ephesus.

questions.question: Is it true that the Greeks supported the Jews in their accusations against Paul?
questions.explanation: The Greeks beat Sosthenes after Gallio's judgment, indicating they did not support the Jews' accusations (Acts 18:17).

hard.title: Acts Chapter 18 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Acts Chapter 18.

questions.question: According to Acts 18:21, what feast was Paul determined to keep in Jerusalem before he sailed from Ephesus?
questions.correctAnswer: The feast that cometh in Jerusalem
questions.explanation: Acts 18:21 states that Paul bade farewell saying, 'I must by all means keep this feast that cometh in Jerusalem,' indicating his determination to keep the upcoming feast in Jerusalem.

questions.question: In Acts 18:22, after landing at Caesarea, where did Paul go next?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:22 explains that after Paul landed at Caesarea and went up to greet the church, he went down to Antioch.

questions.question: What regions did Paul travel through to strengthen the disciples as described in Acts 18:23?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:23 says Paul went over all the country of Galatia and Phrygia to strengthen all the disciples.

questions.question: Who was Apollos, mentioned in Acts 18:24, and what characteristics are attributed to him?
options: A Jew born in Alexandria, eloquent and mighty in the scriptures
A Gentile from Corinth, skilled in rhetoric
A Samaritan prophet, zealous but unlearned
A Roman centurion, strong in faith
questions.correctAnswer: A Jew born in Alexandria, eloquent and mighty in the scriptures
questions.explanation: Acts 18:24 describes Apollos as a Jew born at Alexandria, eloquent, and mighty in the scriptures.

questions.question: According to Acts 18:25, what limitation did Apollos have in his teaching about baptism?
options: He only knew the baptism of John
He emphasized baptism in the Holy Spirit only
questions.correctAnswer: He only knew the baptism of John
questions.explanation: Acts 18:25 states that Apollos was fervent in spirit and taught diligently, but he knew only the baptism of John.

questions.question: What role did Aquila and Priscilla play in Acts 18:26 regarding Apollos' understanding?
options: They expelled him from the synagogue
They took him aside and expounded the way of God more perfectly
They sent him away to Achaia
questions.correctAnswer: They took him aside and expounded the way of God more perfectly
questions.explanation: Acts 18:26 says Aquila and Priscilla heard Apollos and took him unto them to expound the way of God more perfectly.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'ἐξελέξατο' (exelexato) used in Acts 18:27 mean?
questions.explanation: In Acts 18:27, the Greek word 'ἐξελέξατο' means 'was disposed' or 'inclined' to go into Achaia, reflecting a deliberate decision or inclination.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Acts 18:6 when Paul 'shakes his raiment' and declares his hands clean?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:6 shows Paul shaking his raiment as a symbolic action indicating separation from responsibility for those rejecting his message.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects to Paul’s public reasoning and proving Jesus as the Christ in Acts 18:28?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:28 describes Apollos convincing Jews by scripture that Jesus was Christ, which connects to Isaiah 53, the prophetic suffering servant passage fulfilled in Jesus.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Paul's journey strengthening disciples in Acts 18:23?
questions.explanation: Romans 15:19-21 reflects Paul's missionary journeys and strengthening of believers, echoing Acts 18:23 where Paul strengthens disciples in Galatia and Phrygia.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Paul’s farewell to the Ephesians in Acts 18:21?
options: The arrival of Apollos at Ephesus
Paul’s refusal to stay longer despite their desire
Paul’s healing of a sick man
questions.correctAnswer: Paul’s refusal to stay longer despite their desire
questions.explanation: Acts 18:20 states the Ephesians desired Paul to stay longer, but he consented not, directly preceding his farewell in Acts 18:21.

questions.question: Which word study related to Acts 18 reveals the meaning of 'mighty' as used in Acts 18:24 describing Apollos?
questions.explanation: The Greek word translated 'mighty' in Acts 18:24 denotes strength in capability or power, especially in scriptural knowledge and eloquence.

questions.question: Which literary technique is demonstrated by the parallelism between Aquila and Priscilla's role and Apollos' teaching in Acts 18:26-28?
questions.explanation: The passage in Acts 18:26-28 shows parallelism by contrasting Aquila and Priscilla’s private instruction with Apollos' public ministry, highlighting complementary roles.

questions.question: How does Paul’s vow mentioned in Acts 18:18 connect with Old Testament Nazarite practices?
options: It is identical to Nazarite vows in Numbers 6
It likely involved a Nazarite vow including hair shaving
It forbade Paul from eating certain foods
It required Paul to build a temple
questions.correctAnswer: It likely involved a Nazarite vow including hair shaving
questions.explanation: Acts 18:18 mentions Paul shaving his head after a vow, indicating a Nazarite-type vow as described in Numbers 6 involving hair shaving upon completion.

questions.question: True or False: Acts 18:28 states that Apollos helped the believers much through works of the law.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:27-28 states Apollos helped those who had believed through grace, not works of the law.

theological.title: Acts Chapter 18 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Acts Chapter 18 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Acts 18:6 teach about human sin and divine judgment?
options: Individuals are responsible for their own rejection of Christ and bear the consequences.
God forces belief upon all people regardless of their response.
Sin is only a social offense and does not affect eternal destiny.
Judgment is deferred until after the resurrection.
questions.correctAnswer: Individuals are responsible for their own rejection of Christ and bear the consequences.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:6 shows Paul declaring, 'Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean,' indicating personal responsibility for rejecting the gospel.

questions.question: What doctrine about the inclusiveness of salvation does Acts 18:8 teach?
options: Faith in Christ is available to both Jewish leaders and entire households.
Only Gentiles can be saved through faith in Christ.
Salvation is restricted to individuals, not families or groups.
Belief in Christ requires adherence to the Mosaic Law.
questions.correctAnswer: Faith in Christ is available to both Jewish leaders and entire households.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:8 records Crispus, the chief ruler of the synagogue, and all his house believing and being baptized, showing salvation extends to families.

questions.question: What doctrine about the Christian mission is taught in Acts 18:10?
options: God's providential presence ensures protection and success in mission.
Missionary work is futile without political power.
Christians should avoid cities with hostile populations.
Human effort alone secures the growth of the church.
questions.correctAnswer: God's providential presence ensures protection and success in mission.
questions.explanation: In Acts 18:10, God tells Paul 'I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee,' demonstrating divine protection in mission.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Acts 18:9 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Acts 18:9 records the Lord's vision reassuring Paul not to fear but to speak boldly, showing God's faithfulness to support His servants.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Acts 18:10 with the promise that 'no man shall set on thee to hurt thee'?
questions.explanation: The promise in Acts 18:10 reflects God's sovereign control over circumstances to protect Paul from harm.

questions.question: How does Acts 18:24-28 connect to the broader New Testament theme of apostolic teaching and church growth?
options: It illustrates the role of gifted teachers like Apollos in strengthening early Christian communities.
It shows that only Paul was authorized to teach the gospel.
It demonstrates a rejection of Scripture in favor of charismatic speech.
It limits church growth to the region of Ephesus only.
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the role of gifted teachers like Apollos in strengthening early Christian communities.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:24-28 introduces Apollos, an eloquent teacher who greatly aids believers, showing the importance of diverse ministries in church expansion.

questions.question: In what way does the conflict in Acts 18:12-17 anticipate later New Testament themes of religious opposition and divine justice?
options: It shows the limitation of human authority in opposing God's work, as Gallio refuses to judge spiritual matters.
It depicts the triumph of Jewish law over the gospel.
It teaches that Christians should avoid all legal confrontations.
It suggests that religious violence is always condoned by God.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows the limitation of human authority in opposing God's work, as Gallio refuses to judge spiritual matters.
questions.explanation: Gallio's refusal in Acts 18:15-16 to judge the gospel matter demonstrates that earthly powers are limited in opposing God's plan.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Acts 18:4 and Acts 18:28 teach about evangelism and scriptural witness?
options: Evangelism must be grounded in Scripture to effectively persuade both Jews and Gentiles.
Evangelism relies solely on personal charisma and not on Scripture.
Scripture is irrelevant to early Christian preaching.
Public persuasion is unnecessary for spreading the gospel.
questions.correctAnswer: Evangelism must be grounded in Scripture to effectively persuade both Jews and Gentiles.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:4 shows Paul reasoning in the synagogue, and Acts 18:28 shows Apollos proving Jesus as Christ from the Scriptures, emphasizing scriptural foundation.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight about the role of the Holy Spirit and instruction is taught by combining Acts 18:25 and Acts 18:26?
options: The Spirit empowers believers but also requires further doctrinal teaching for completeness.
The Spirit alone is sufficient without need for instruction.
Instruction is unnecessary and may hinder spiritual fervor.
The Spirit only works through the Apostle Paul.
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit empowers believers but also requires further doctrinal teaching for completeness.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:25 describes Apollos as fervent in spirit but knowing only John's baptism, while 18:26 shows Priscilla and Aquila instructing him more perfectly.

questions.question: What theological synthesis about Christian fellowship and mission does Acts 18:18 and Acts 18:19 provide?
options: Missionary work is supported and accompanied by close fellowship with fellow believers like Priscilla and Aquila.
Missionaries must always work alone without companions.
Fellowship is unrelated to mission effectiveness.
Mission is primarily a political act rather than spiritual.
questions.correctAnswer: Missionary work is supported and accompanied by close fellowship with fellow believers like Priscilla and Aquila.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:18 and 18:19 show Paul traveling with Priscilla and Aquila and leaving them in Ephesus, highlighting partnership in mission.

questions.question: Sceptics claim Acts 18:12-17 shows the Roman authorities suppressing Christianity. What does this passage actually teach?
options: Roman authorities like Gallio maintain neutrality and do not judge religious disputes.
The Roman government actively persecutes all Christians.
The state fully endorses the Jewish opposition to Paul.
Christianity was officially banned by Gallio.
questions.correctAnswer: Roman authorities like Gallio maintain neutrality and do not judge religious disputes.
questions.explanation: Gallio refuses to adjudicate the Jews' complaint against Paul in Acts 18:15, indicating Roman officials did not interfere in religious debates.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of Christian vocation is taught in Acts 18:3?
options: Christian workers are called to both manual labor and ministry simultaneously.
Ministry must be full-time with no other occupations.
Tentmaking is a metaphor for spiritual warfare only.
questions.correctAnswer: Christian workers are called to both manual labor and ministry simultaneously.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:3 shows Paul working as a tentmaker with Aquila and Priscilla, combining labor with ministry.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is illustrated by God’s promise in Acts 18:21 that Paul will return to Ephesus 'if God will'?
questions.explanation: Paul’s conditional statement in Acts 18:21 acknowledges God's sovereign control over future events.

questions.question: How does Acts 18:23 relate to the New Testament theme of edification and pastoral care?
options: It emphasizes strengthening and encouraging disciples through systematic pastoral oversight.
It teaches that discipleship is primarily self-directed without leadership.
It rejects regional ministry in favor of centralized control.
It focuses only on evangelism without follow-up.
questions.correctAnswer: It emphasizes strengthening and encouraging disciples through systematic pastoral oversight.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:23 shows Paul traveling through Galatia and Phrygia to strengthen disciples, reflecting pastoral care.

questions.question: What theological principle about baptism can be inferred from Acts 18:25 regarding Apollos’ understanding?
options: Baptism must be doctrinally understood, as Apollos initially knew only John’s baptism.
Baptism is purely symbolic with no need for correct teaching.
John's baptism is superior to Christian baptism.
questions.correctAnswer: Baptism must be doctrinally understood, as Apollos initially knew only John’s baptism.
questions.explanation: Acts 18:25 notes Apollos was 'knowing only the baptism of John,' implying incomplete understanding necessitating further instruction.
